tldr: Wealthsimple dominated the news with its 'Wealthsimple Presents' launch: the Penny AI assistant, instant Wealthsimple Pay transfers, commission-free CAD options and a CADD stablecoin. Meanwhile, the Big Five Canadian banks are blocking third-party AI agents and BMO is putting agentic AI into its contact centre.
themes: AI assistants and agents, in-app and in the contact centre
Wealthsimple's push into trading, payments and crypto
Big banks restricting third-party AI agent access
Card rewards and cash back competition
Crypto and stablecoin access, with some operational risk

highlights.headline: Wealthsimple launched Penny, an AI assistant that prepares e-transfers, invoice payments and trades, always with client confirmation. ChatGPT and Claude connections are planned. It also launched Wealthsimple Pay (instant transfers up to $100K between clients) and temporary virtual cards.
highlights.why: This is the most direct competitive move for Simplii's DIY audience. It raises the bar for in-app AI and payments, and Simplii's Folders and payment backup pilots now look modest next to it.

highlights.headline: Wealthsimple went live with commission-free options on Canadian stocks, with Wealthsimple Pro (Level 2 data) due late November. It also announced the CADD CAD stablecoin with a 3.25% annual reward and a business credit card (no FX fees, 1% cash back) for early 2027.
highlights.why: Wealthsimple is widening its lead with self-directed investors, which matters for Simplii's CIBC Investor's Edge partnership. The 3.25% stablecoin reward also adds a new yield option to compare with savings rates.

highlights.headline: RBC, TD, BMO and CIBC are blocking or limiting third-party AI agents from authenticated online banking, and Scotiabank is 'limiting' them. RBC's CEO cited fraud and consumer-harm risks.
highlights.why: Simplii, as part of CIBC, will likely face the same policy question. Wealthsimple's Penny plans to connect to ChatGPT and Claude, so the access stance is a live strategic choice.

highlights.headline: RBC overhauled its Cash Back Mastercard line with uncapped 3% categories (effective Oct 1) and $1 redemptions from December. BMO also launched AI Agent Assist for credit card service, targeting up to 30% shorter call times.
highlights.why: The rewards bar is moving up at a direct competitor, and BMO is using AI to cut service costs. Both are benchmarks for Simplii's card value proposition and service efficiency.
